findings.finding: The plan blames test_run_git_wrapper::test_str_input_is_forwarded_to_stdin only on run_git's text-mode stdin. But the test's comparison side is also a text-mode write: `(repo / "probe").write_text(content)`. On Windows that writes CRLF to the probe file. After the run_git fix, the piped hash covers LF bytes. The direct `git hash-object <path>` hash only matches if git's core.autocrlf=true clean filter turns the probe's CRLF back into LF. So the test passing after the fix rests on an unstated premise about runner git config, not on the product fix alone. test_run_git_wrapper.py is also not in Scope.
scenarios: A Windows runner or dev box with core.autocrlf=false or input: after the fix, piped hashes 'hello from stdin\n' while direct hashes the CRLF probe file. The test still fails even though the product fix is correct.
The Windows validation run passes only because the runner's system git config has autocrlf=true. The test then stays green by coincidence and breaks silently if the runner image changes.
findings.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/test_run_git_wrapper.py, write the probe with `(repo / "probe").write_bytes(content.encode("utf-8"))` and hash it with `run_git(repo, "hash-object", "--no-filters", str(repo / "probe"))`. Then the expected hash is the LF bytes on every platform and config. Add the file to Scope.

findings.finding: The plan names `test_run_git_wrapper::test_str_input_is_forwarded_to_stdin` as sub-cause 1's oracle and leaves the test unchanged. That test builds its comparison hash from `(repo / "probe").write_text(content)`, which writes CRLF on Windows. `git hash-object <path>` then applies the autocrlf clean filter. After the fix, the test passes on Windows only because Git for Windows' system core.autocrlf=true happens to turn the probe's CRLF back into LF. On any Windows environment where autocrlf is unset, false, or input-only, the direct hash covers CRLF bytes while the fixed piped hash covers LF, so the test fails even though run_git is now correct.
